title: Conditions of Payment for PBM Services Agreement Invoices
content:
These conditions govern when a plan sponsor's invoices under its PBM Services Agreement fall due, how payments are applied, when late payment interest is charged and how the claims funding deposit is held. The amount the sponsor owes Northbridge Rx for claims and fees is its receivable: invoices and late charges raise it, and payments and credit memos lower it.

## Clause 1 — Due date and application of payments

Each invoice is due the number of calendar days set by the arrangement's payment terms after its invoice date. A payment is applied to the invoice it names.

## Clause 2 — Late payment interest

Late interest at the arrangement's monthly late payment interest rate is charged on the unpaid amount of an invoice only once the arrangement's grace period, in calendar days, has passed after its due date, the due date being day zero, and at most once per invoice per calendar month.

2.1 *Counting.* The due date is day zero; the following calendar day is day 1. The grace period has passed only once the count is beyond the number of grace days: on the day whose number equals the grace days, the grace period has not yet passed; from the next day onward it has. Calendar days are counted, not business days. The due date shown on the invoice record is the date counted from.

2.2 *Amount.* One month's late interest on an invoice is the unpaid amount of that invoice multiplied by the monthly rate.

2.3 *Frequency.* An invoice bears late interest at most once in any calendar month.

| Day relative to the due date (grace period of 5 calendar days) | Late interest chargeable on the unpaid amount |
|---|---|
| Day 0 (the due date) to day 4 | No |
| Day 5 | No — the grace period has not yet passed |
| Day 6 and later | Yes, at most once per invoice per calendar month |

## Clause 3 — Claims funding deposit

A claims funding deposit equal to the arrangement's number of weeks of average claims cost is held. It is not applied to invoices until the agreement ends.

## Illustrations (hypothetical inputs)

- *Due date.* An invoice dated on day 0 under hypothetical payment terms of 10 calendar days is due on day 10.
- *Interest.* An invoice with a hypothetical unpaid amount of 20000.00 USD, under a hypothetical monthly rate of 1.5%, bears late interest of 20000.00 multiplied by 0.015, that is 300.00 USD, for a calendar month in which the grace period has passed; a second charge on that invoice in the same calendar month is not made.
- *Partly paid invoice.* A payment naming the invoice reduces its unpaid amount; interest is charged on the amount still unpaid, not on the original invoice amount.
- *Deposit.* While the agreement continues, the deposit is not used to settle any invoice, however overdue.
